verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against Yahweh, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
or has found that which was lost, and dealt falsely therein, and swearing to a lie; in any of these things that a man does, sinning therein;

then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,

or any thing about which he has sworn falsely; he shall restore it even in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. To him to whom it belongs he shall give it, in the day of his being found guilty.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Yahweh, a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
The priest shall make atonement for him before Yahweh, and he will be forgiven concerning whatever he does to become guilty.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put on his linen breeches upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
He shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it, it shall not go out; and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning: and he shall lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
“‘This is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Yahweh, before the altar.

He shall take from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal offering, and of its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the meal offering, and shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma, as its memorial, to Yahweh.
That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten without yeast in a holy place. They shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire. It is most holy, as the sin offering, and as the trespass offering.
Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it, as their portion forever throughout your generations, from the offerings of Yahweh made by fire. Whoever touches them shall be holy.’”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

“This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons, which they shall offer to Yahweh in the day when he is anointed: one tenth of an ephah  of fine flour for a meal offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening.
It shall be made with oil in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bring it in. You shall offer the meal offering in baked pieces for a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
The anointed priest that will be in his place from among his sons shall offer it. By a statute forever, it shall be wholly burned to Yahweh.
Every meal offering of a priest shall be wholly burned. It shall not be eaten.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before Yahweh. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Meeting.
Whatever shall touch its flesh shall be holy. When there is any of its blood sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled in a holy place.
But the earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water.
Every male among the priests shall eat of it: it is most holy.
No sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten: it shall be burned with fire.

footnotes.content: God speaks again through Moses—this time about broken trust. Notice the pattern: He always moves toward restoration, even in sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The catalog is specific: theft, false witness, broken deposit—sin wears many faces, but they all orbit one center: we take what isn't ours. The Lord names them all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To take a lost thing and swear falsely about it—that's where conscience goes quiet. We pretend we found nothing, that we know nothing, that we are nothing to answer for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Restoration is not soft: the guilty person must return the exact thing taken, or equivalent value. Grace has muscle. The Lord doesn't erase the wrong; He asks it be made right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One fifth more—restitution plus interest. The extra acknowledges harm done and honor broken. Only then, publicly and fully, can forgiveness mean something real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A ram without defect—the person brings their best to undo their worst. The offering cost something. This is how we show that we understand what we broke.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest makes atonement. He stands between God and the guilty one—foreshadowing the One who will stand for all of us, bearing our false dealings to the Father.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again the Lord speaks to Moses: the rhythm of instruction, the patience of His teaching. He wants His people to understand the weight of their work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The burnt offering kept burning all night—a prayer in ash and flame. The priest feeds that fire every morning, saying with his hands: this offering never sleeps, never stops ascending.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Linen garments for the living work, linen for touching what is burned—the priesthood dressed itself in the work of drawing near. Every fabric declared: this is holy ground.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Change garments, carry the ashes out. Even what remains from the offering must be treated with care and removed to clean ground. Nothing profane touches what has been sacred.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire kept burning—the priest tends it like a shepherd tends his flock, morning after morning. This is the work of constancy, the priesthood in its dailiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Continual fire—the law speaks in absolutes because prayer speaks in absolutes. The altar's flames were the people's praise kept alive while they slept and worked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The meal offering now—grain and oil, the work of hands and harvest brought before the Lord. Not blood-guilt, but the fruit of labor, offered and remembered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A handful becomes memorial—the priest takes the finest part, the frankincense rises, and ordinary grain becomes a pleasing aroma to the Lord. Small acts, received with delight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What remains feeds Aaron's house—the gift returns as sustenance. To serve the Lord is to be provided for. The altar's work is not separate from daily bread.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Most holy, like the sin offering—the meal offering and the guilt offering stand together in their sanctity. Both speak to God's nearness in sorrow and in simple thankfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every male of Aaron's line, forever—the priesthood is not a privilege to be earned once but a station to be kept holy, generation after generation, through the eating of holy bread.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses listens yet again—the Lord's instruction is patient and thorough, because His house deserves utter clarity and the priesthood must know exactly what it means to stand for others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The high priest's own offering, split between dawn and dark—a daily sacrifice that mirrors the offering of the people, but he can never stop offering for himself. The mediator, too, needs the altar.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mixed with oil, baked in pieces, brought as a daily gift—the high priest's offering is humble and tangible, no different in its offering than the common meal. His prayer rises in grain and fire.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anointed priest, then his successor—the office passes, but the offering never stops. This is succession as continuity, not as escape. The high priest's son inherits a fire to keep burning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every meal offering from a priest, wholly burned—wholly. The high priest cannot take his own offering home. What he brings must be consumed completely, a sign that his vow is absolute.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sin offering now—Aaron and his sons are told the law. Again and again the Lord teaches what it means to carry the guilt of others, to stand where they cannot stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Most holy—the sin offering shares the holiness of the burnt offering, because where sin is named, the Lord's presence intensifies. He draws near most closely where the wound runs deepest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest eats it in a holy place—he consumes the burden he has lifted. The sin offering is not removed from sight; it is internalized, carried in the body of the one who bears it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whatever touches its flesh becomes holy—the sin offering sanctifies everything around it. Holiness spreads through contact, because where guilt is addressed, the Lord's purifying work begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Earthen vessels broken, bronze vessels cleansed—the vessel that touches the sin offering cannot be the same. Some things, once used for holy work, must be destroyed or remade entirely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every male priest, most holy—the burden is shared among the priesthood, but only the ordained can eat. To consume the sin offering is to step into a covenant too weighty for words.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: the sin offering brought into the Holy Place—that spoke of a Day when One would enter the inner sanctuary bearing all our breaking, burning away what we could never remove ourselves. We still live in the light of that offering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
